one_liner: Header-only C++ HTTP server and async SQL toolkit on fibers; beat actix-web on TechEmpower DB tests only in Round 20.
what_it_does: Lithium is a set of C++ libraries shipped as single headers: HTTP server, HTTP client, JSON, async PostgreSQL/MySQL, SQLite and a small ORM. You declare routes on an li::http_api with lambdas taking http_request/http_response, then call li::http_serve(api, port). Field names are compile-time symbols (s::name) that drive JSON encoding, parameter parsing and ORM columns without runtime reflection. It is a whole framework with its own API, not a drop-in for actix-web or any other server.
how_it_is_fast: Each worker thread runs its own edge-triggered epoll reactor (kqueue on macOS) on one shared listening socket. Every connection is a boost::context continuation (stackful coroutine), so handlers read like blocking code while socket and libpq I/O yield to the reactor. Responses collect in a 50 KB output buffer that is flushed only when the input buffer is empty, so HTTP/1.1-pipelined responses leave in one send; a helper thread rebuilds the Date header once per second. PostgreSQL uses non-blocking libpq with a per-connection prepared-statement cache. The Round 20 winner also pipelined queries from many requests over one connection per thread, using the pre-release libpq batch patch (v22) and clang -O3 -march=native -flto with two-pass PGO.
when_to_use: Linux HTTP/1.1 service where you want top-tier plaintext/JSON throughput from a small C++ code base you can vendor as one header (Round 20: about 7.0M plaintext and 1.6M JSON req/s, network-bound).
Handlers that run simple PostgreSQL or MySQL queries, where you want async DB I/O written as straight-line code on fibers instead of callbacks or C++20 coroutines.
Prototyping JSON REST APIs in C++ with compile-time, symbol-based JSON binding, sessions and a small ORM, if a one-maintainer project is acceptable.
Studying HTTP and DB pipelining in C++: the TechEmpower code and the libpq batch experiments are public and short.
when_not_to_use: When DB-bound throughput against actix-web decides: in TechEmpower Rounds 21-22 Lithium reaches 0.66x-0.91x of actix-http on single query, 20 queries, Fortunes and updates, and it is below H2O on all DB tests in Rounds 22-23.

Internet-facing services that need a hardened parser: a high-severity JSON stack-exhaustion DoS (GHSA-cv26-62rq-922g) was fixed only on 2026-04-21, more security fixes landed 2026-07-31, and a HashDoS report on hashmap_http_session (#138) is open.
Workloads with one request per connection: open issue #122 (2022, no reply) reports slow responses and low CPU use once clients stop reusing keep-alive connections.
Windows (README: not supported; only unsupported wepoll code paths exist), and PostgreSQL on macOS, where connection setup falls back to a blocking PQconnectdb on the reactor thread.
Need for HTTP/2, HTTP/3 or WebSocket: there is no code or documentation for them in the repository.

integration.dependencies: Boost.Context and Boost.LexicalCast, OpenSSL; libpq for PostgreSQL, MariaDB client for MySQL, SQLite3, libcurl for the HTTP client; optional li_symbol_generator tool to declare s:: symbols
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (TechEmpower builds use -std=c++17; the repo's CMake now sets C++20); documented compilers G++ 9.2, Clang++ 9.0, Apple clang 12
integration.platforms: Linux (epoll, primary target), macOS (kqueue); Windows not supported per README
integration.thread_safety: One reactor per thread, each with its own fibers; handlers on different threads run concurrently, so shared state captured by handler lambdas needs your own locking. SQL connection pools are documented as thread-safe; async pools are per thread (max_async_connections_per_thread).

gotchas: The docs name the thread-count option s::threads, but http_serve reads s::nthreads, so the documented option has no effect and the server uses hardware_concurrency threads.
Fibers are cooperative: a blocking call in a handler (file read, synchronous DB connection, sleep) stalls every connection on that reactor thread.
You must declare symbols (by hand or with li_symbol_generator), and programs with several translation units need #define LI_EXTERN_GLOBALS in all but one file to avoid duplicate SQL globals.

The README and docs still claim '#1 on TechEmpower (composite score)'. That rests on the pipelined batch variant, which the author himself removed from TechEmpower in May 2022 to comply with the benchmark rules.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Lithium over Drogon or Crow when you want a single-header framework with synchronous-looking fiber handlers and compile-time JSON/ORM binding, and can accept a one-maintainer project. For DB-heavy work, current TechEmpower data puts H2O and actix-web ahead of it.
verified_claims_summary: TechEmpower Round 20 ran on Citrine: three Xeon Gold 5120 servers on 10 GbE. There lithium-postgres-batch (clang/LLVM 10, -O3 -march=native -flto, PGO, patched libpq) beat actix-core (Rust 1.44, target-cpu=native) by 1.31x on single query, about 1.7x on 20 queries and 1.44x on 20-query updates; Fortunes was a tie (0.95x-1.01x, depending on the time base) and JSON/plaintext were about equal. This is a historical result: the batch variant was withdrawn in 2022, and in Rounds 21-22 non-batched Lithium trails actix-http on every DB test.
status_note: Active (security and vcpkg fixes through 2026-07-31), MIT-licensed and header-only, so it is easy to vendor; it has one main maintainer and no tagged releases.
